premises.text: Applications with related data are forced to store it in unrelated, separately controlled databases
premises.evidence_span: applications that had related data no longer were forced to store it into unrelated databases

premises.text: FluidDB is a shared writable database where any application can add information to shared objects without asking permission
premises.evidence_span: It's a shared database for applications

premises.text: When independent apps store related data in the same place, unanticipated cross-app queries become trivial
premises.evidence_span: I've combined data in an unanticipated way from three independent but related applications

premises.text: FluidDB provides a shared writable object for everything—a platform for the web of things
premises.evidence_span: FluidDB gives you a shared, writable object for everything

value.text: Related information lives together so applications and people can add and combine data without permission gates
value.evidence_span: they're choosing to store their information into a place that makes it more valuable, because it's more useful

secondary_value.text: A writable, social future of data not controlled solely by applications
secondary_value.evidence_span: The future of data is a writable future

causal_links.evidence_span: when the information is in the same place, it becomes trivial
combining data from two different databases, is very difficult in the normal world
none of them had to ask permission to put that information into FluidDB

notes: Tickery/TunkRank/We Met At demos treated as evidence of the shared-DB mechanism, not separate product premises. 'Future of data' vision recorded in secondary_value per §4.1.4 rather than as a premise. Funding anecdote excluded. P4 web-of-things scope kept inside the platform domain as the same writable-object mechanism at universal scope.
